plugin.agenda.desc: Agenda: the character plans two to four things for itself each day, goes and does them at the appointed time and brings back a line about how it went; dated commitments are kept separately and folded into the day's plan when their day comes
plugin.agenda.field.auto_plan.desc: After the first turn of a new day (or the first heartbeat), let the character draw up its own plan for the day. Turn this off to keep only commitments and hand-edited plans.
plugin.agenda.field.auto_plan.label: Plan each day automatically
plugin.agenda.field.day_start_hour.desc: Anything before this belongs to the previous day: still chatting at 1 a.m. is not a new day.
plugin.agenda.field.day_start_hour.label: Hour a new day starts
plugin.agenda.field.max_commitments_inje: Upcoming commitments are injected soonest-first up to this many; the rest are noted as a count and can be read with list_commitments.
plugin.agenda.field.max_inject_bytes.des: Combined limit for today's plan and upcoming commitments. Over the limit, the notes on finished items go first, then finished items collapse into a count, and finally commitments are reduced to a count; whatever is in progress and whatever comes next are always kept.
plugin.agenda.field.max_items.desc: Upper bound when planning. The prompt asks for two to four things with plenty of empty space; this is the hard ceiling.
plugin.agenda.field.max_items.label: Most items in a day
plugin.agenda.field.remind_before_minute: How long before a commitment with you to hand the heartbeat a reason to speak up. 0 means never.
plugin.agenda.field.run_activities.desc: When an item's time arrives, run a turn on the most recently active session so the character decides whether to go, and another when it gets back to write down how it went. Turn this off to only inject the plan.
plugin.agenda.field.run_activities.label: Run start / end turns automatically
A start turn dispatched within this long of the appointed time counts as on time; later than that, the turn says how late it is.
plugin.belongings.desc: Belongings: what is in the fridge, the wardrobe and other containers, kept as a list that changes with the story and survives compaction and new sessions
plugin.belongings.field.max_containers.d: How many containers (fridge, wardrobe and the like) may exist at once.
plugin.belongings.field.max_inject_bytes: The list is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, items collapse into counts; over it still, only the number of containers is noted.
plugin.belongings.field.max_items.desc: Past this, putting things in is refused with a nudge to clear some out. A belongings list should not grow into a warehouse ledger.
plugin.belongings.field.max_items.label: Item limit per container
plugin.body_sense.desc: Body awareness: counts how often each part has been touched and gives reaction guidance by familiarity stage, alongside arousal and fatigue that ebb with time
plugin.body_sense.field.arousal_decay_pe: How many points arousal (0-100) falls back toward 0 each hour — the falling itself is the afterglow. 0 means no decay, and arousal stays wherever it was left.
plugin.body_sense.field.familiarity_pace: Scales how fast the stages advance. At the middle setting: 1 time is the first, 2-3 is unfamiliar, 4-9 is getting used to it, 10-19 is familiar, 20 and up is second nature.
plugin.body_sense.field.fatigue_decay_pe: How many points fatigue (0-100) falls back toward 0 each hour — rest recovers on its own. 0 means no decay.
plugin.body_sense.field.max_inject_bytes: The record is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, counts are dropped and only stages remain, then parts are merged by stage; over it still, only the number of parts is noted.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_close.desc: One part per line. Contact that needs an established closeness before it stops being abrupt.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_daily.desc: One part per line. Contact that can happen between strangers or ordinary friends, and becomes routine after a few times.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_intimate.d: One part per line. Contact that only happens in an explicitly intimate relationship; it keeps its charge however often it happens.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_private.de: One part per line. The more entries here, the more readily the model reports into this tier — keep only the few that are truly necessary.
plugin.body_sense.field.state_max_delta_: How much one call may move arousal or fatigue. Anything beyond is clamped, and the model is told so.
Largest single change to body state
plugin.dual_persona.desc: Dual persona: an outer and an inner self, with the inner one's conversations and memories invisible to the outer; trigger phrases switch between them
With split channels on, the inner persona's replies go to this channel. Pick a channel that is enabled and where you have already talked to the bot. Replies that cannot be delivered are dropped, with a note left in the session.
Unset (reply where the message came from)
Injected only while the inner persona is active, and it takes precedence over the outer character sheet. Nothing about it is injected in outer mode.
plugin.dual_persona.field.inner_voice_sa: Injected only while the inner persona is active. Samples of how it actually talks, to anchor the voice: three to five exchanges works well, each a back and forth (what you say, how it answers), covering different moods, with a blank line between them. If the outer persona has sample lines, give the inner one a set too — otherwise its voice drifts toward the outer samples.
plugin.dual_persona.field.match_mode.des: Contains: the phrase appearing anywhere in the message triggers it. Whole message: only a message that is exactly the phrase triggers it, which is much harder to set off by accident.
plugin.dual_persona.field.max_text_bytes: Combined limit for the inner persona sheet and its sample lines. They are resent on every inner-persona turn and never hit the prompt cache; over the limit the sheet is kept first and samples are dropped one block at a time.
With split channels on, the outer persona's replies go to this channel. Pick a channel that is enabled and where you have already talked to the bot. Replies that cannot be delivered are dropped, with a note left in the session.
Unset (reply where the message came from)
plugin.dual_persona.field.split_channels: With this on, a reply goes to the channel that belongs to the current persona, no matter which channel you spoke through: say the switch phrase on QQ and the side that takes over answers you on WeChat. Both fields below need an enabled channel. With it off, replies always go back the way they came.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_inner.desc: One per line; any match switches. The matching message is sent to the model as usual and answered by the new persona, with no announcement.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_inner.label: Phrases that switch to the inner persona
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_outer.desc: One per line. The switch takes effect within the same turn, so this phrase stays in the history the outer persona can read — pick something that also makes sense in its company.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_outer.label: Phrases that switch back to the outer persona
plugin.exec_command.desc: Runs shell commands in the working directory, with dangerous ones held for your confirmation
plugin.exec_command.field.confirm_timeou: No answer within this long counts as a refusal.
plugin.exec_command.field.guard.desc: Dangerous: deleting, overwriting, rewriting history, changing system settings and the like are held for your confirmation, everything else runs (recommended). All: everything but read-only commands is confirmed. Off: nothing is held. Note that this reads the command text, so it catches mistakes but not deliberate obfuscation — only the "all" setting is airtight.
plugin.exec_command.field.guard.label: Dangerous command guard
plugin.exec_command.field.timeout_second: Longest a single command may run; after that it is killed and whatever it printed is handed back to the model.
plugin.feishu_bot.desc: Connects a Feishu bot for remote one-to-one sessions (events over a long-lived connection, no public address needed), with /new /status /compact /help and remote confirmation of dangerous operations
plugin.feishu_bot.field.api_base.desc: Rarely needs changing; set it for a self-hosted deployment — the long-lived connection follows it too
plugin.feishu_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.feishu_bot.field.app_id.desc: From a custom app created in the Feishu developer console (https://open.feishu.cn/app); looks like cli_xxx
plugin.feishu_bot.field.app_id.label: App ID
plugin.feishu_bot.field.app_secret.desc: The app credential. It is kept on this machine only and never uploaded anywhere. Note that Feishu and Lark credentials are not interchangeable
plugin.feishu_bot.field.app_secret.label: App Secret
plugin.feishu_bot.field.confirm_timeout_: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.feishu_bot.field.format.desc: Feishu plain text messages do not render markdown, so sending it raw fills the screen with asterisks. Card: sent as a rich card, where bold, links and code render properly. Plain text: converted to readable plain text before sending
plugin.feishu_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.feishu_bot.field.human_pace.desc: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.feishu_bot.field.human_pace.label: Text like a person
plugin.feishu_bot.field.merge_window_sec: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.feishu_bot.field.push_notices.des: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
plugin.feishu_bot.field.show_thinking.de: Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.feishu_bot.field.show_tools.desc: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.feishu_bot.field.show_tools.label: Show tool calls
plugin.feishu_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One open_id per line (looks like ou_xxx); only listed users get a reply, and an empty list refuses everyone. The first time a stranger writes, their open_id is written to the log so you can copy it in
plugin.feishu_bot.field.whitelist.label: open_id allowlist
plugin.health.desc: Health: the character catches something minor now and then, the model decides from the story whether it falls ill, and the illness rises and fades over time, injected each turn and coloring how it speaks
plugin.health.field.cooldown_days.desc: No new condition may be recorded for this many days after the last recovery; the tool refuses and explains the rule. This is the hard brake on the appetite for drama — without it the character is ill every other day.
plugin.health.field.cooldown_days.label: Cooldown after recovery (days)
plugin.health.field.max_conditions.desc: How many conditions may be on record at the same time; beyond that, recording is refused. A minor ailment is usually one; a chill with a headache is two.
plugin.health.field.max_conditions.label: Conditions at once
plugin.health.field.max_severity.desc: The worst it may get. Anything the model reports above this is clamped, and the model is told so.
plugin.health.field.max_severity.label: Severity ceiling
plugin.heartbeat.desc: Wakes the model on a timer to run the heartbeat prompt on the most recently active session; the character can set its own pace from how the conversation is going
plugin.heartbeat.field.context_prompts.d: Different heartbeat prompts for different situations. Start each block with "[name]" on a line of its own, followed by that situation's content; you can write several (say [bedtime] [small talk] [working]). The character switches between them itself, and saying "default" goes back to the prompt above. One situation, "life", ships as an example (the character living its own day when nobody is around); edit or delete it freely. Leave this empty to always use the prompt above.
plugin.heartbeat.field.dynamic.desc: Lets the character set when it next speaks up, or pause for a while, and slows the pace step by step toward the longest interval when nobody is talking. Turn it off for a fixed interval the character cannot change
plugin.heartbeat.field.dynamic.label: Dynamic heartbeat
The interval to start from after enabling or reconfiguring
plugin.heartbeat.field.max_minutes.desc: The ceiling both for the character slowing itself down and for the automatic slowdown when nobody is talking
plugin.heartbeat.field.max_minutes.label: Longest interval (minutes)
plugin.heartbeat.field.min_minutes.desc: However eager the character gets, it cannot go below this
plugin.heartbeat.field.min_minutes.label: Shortest interval (minutes)
plugin.heartbeat.field.prompt.desc: What each heartbeat sends as its input, alongside the system prompt and the prompts of every enabled plugin. How long it has been since the last conversation is appended automatically, so there is no need to write vague phrasing like "it has been a while" yourself
plugin.heartbeat.field.prompt.label: Heartbeat prompt
plugin.lark_bot.desc: Connects a Lark bot for remote one-to-one sessions (events over a long-lived connection, no public address needed), with /new /status /compact /help and remote confirmation of dangerous operations
plugin.lark_bot.field.api_base.desc: Rarely needs changing; set it for a self-hosted deployment — the long-lived connection follows it too
plugin.lark_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.lark_bot.field.app_id.desc: From a custom app created in the Lark developer console (https://open.larksuite.com/app); looks like cli_xxx
plugin.lark_bot.field.app_id.label: App ID
plugin.lark_bot.field.app_secret.desc: The app credential. It is kept on this machine only and never uploaded anywhere. Note that Lark and Feishu credentials are not interchangeable
plugin.lark_bot.field.app_secret.label: App Secret
plugin.lark_bot.field.confirm_timeout_se: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.lark_bot.field.format.desc: Lark plain text messages do not render markdown, so sending it raw fills the screen with asterisks. Card: sent as a rich card, where bold, links and code render properly. Plain text: converted to readable plain text before sending
plugin.lark_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.lark_bot.field.human_pace.desc: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.lark_bot.field.human_pace.label: Text like a person
plugin.lark_bot.field.merge_window_sec.d: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.lark_bot.field.push_notices.desc: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
plugin.lark_bot.field.push_notices.label: Push background notices
plugin.lark_bot.field.show_thinking.desc: Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.lark_bot.field.show_tools.desc: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.lark_bot.field.show_tools.label: Show tool calls
plugin.lark_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One open_id per line (looks like ou_xxx); only listed users get a reply, and an empty list refuses everyone. The first time a stranger writes, their open_id is written to the log so you can copy it in
plugin.lark_bot.field.whitelist.label: open_id allowlist
plugin.memory.desc: Long-term memory across sessions; the index rides along with the conversation and full entries are read on demand
plugin.memory.field.auto_extract.desc: Before the session history is replaced by a summary, spend one separate model call pulling out the conclusions worth keeping. With this off, memories are only saved when the character thinks to save them. Each compaction therefore costs one extra model call.
plugin.memory.field.auto_extract.label: Distil memories when compacting
plugin.memory.field.decay.desc: Lets memories marked as forgettable lose their hold over time: after long enough without a mention the body collapses into a single point, and later still the entry leaves the library (moved into a forgotten folder inside it, never actually deleted). Whether an entry can fade is decided one by one as it is saved; unmarked memories are kept forever and this switch does not touch them.
plugin.memory.field.decay.label: Let memories fade
plugin.memory.field.decay_blur_days.desc: How many days a forgettable memory can go unmentioned before its detail is lost and only the gist remains.
plugin.memory.field.decay_forget_days.de: How many days a forgettable memory can go unmentioned before it leaves the library. Must be greater than the days until detail fades.
plugin.memory.field.decay_forget_days.la: Days until it leaves the library
plugin.memory.field.max_entry_bytes.desc: Reading a memory in full truncates anything past this.
plugin.memory.field.max_extract.desc: Anything beyond is dropped, so one distillation cannot flood the library with low-value entries.
plugin.memory.field.max_extract.label: Memories per distillation
plugin.memory.field.max_index_bytes.desc: The index is resent on every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, the per-entry summaries are dropped and only titles remain; over it still, the list is truncated.
plugin.memory.field.max_index_entries.de: Past this, the most recently updated are kept; the rest are still readable by the model and nothing is lost.
plugin.memory.field.recall_entry_runes.d: A recalled memory is truncated past this length; the full text can still be read later by title.
plugin.memory.field.recall_max.desc: Each turn, the words in what you just said pick out the most relevant memories and hand their text straight to the character — the way you remember something because it came up, rather than going to look it up. Plain word matching, no extra model call. 0 turns it off.
plugin.memory.field.recall_max.label: Memories recalled per turn
plugin.memory.field.recall_max_bytes.des: Everything recalled in one turn stays under this many bytes; entries that do not fit give way. This block is resent every turn and never hits the cache, so do not set it high.
plugin.memory.field.recall_min_score.des: How related a memory has to be before it comes to mind: a word matched in the title or summary scores 3, a word matched in the body scores 1; with nothing matched in the title or summary, the body needs 4 matching words. Lower recalls more readily, and misremembers more readily too.
plugin.memory.field.scope.desc: Global: one library shared by every working directory, kept in the config directory. Per project: kept in .wen/memories/ under the working directory, invisible between projects (worth adding to that project's .gitignore). Switching does not move what is already stored.
plugin.memory.field.scope.label: Library scope
plugin.memory.field.timeline.desc: Folds each day's conversations into one "date | what happened" line the following day; the last few ride along with the conversation and answer "what have we been up to lately". Costs one model call per calendar day that had conversation.
plugin.memory.field.timeline.label: Daily timeline
plugin.memory.field.timeline_days.desc: How many recent timeline lines ride along with the conversation; older ones stay in the library without being injected.
plugin.memory.field.timeline_days.label: Timeline entries injected
plugin.memory.field.turn_extract.desc: Every so many turns, spend one separate model call pulling the conclusions worth keeping out of that stretch of conversation, revising any old memory it contradicts along the way. No need to wait for a compaction — most conversations never get that far. Each distillation window therefore costs one extra model call.
plugin.memory.field.turn_extract.label: Distil memories during a conversation
plugin.memory.field.turn_extract_every.d: How many turns of real conversation between distillations. Turns the machine starts on its own (heartbeats, scheduled tasks) do not count. If more than half an hour has passed since the last exchange, whatever has piled up is distilled before going on.
plugin.mood.desc: Mood: how the character feels right now, moved by what happens between you and drifting back toward calm over time, injected each turn and coloring how it speaks
plugin.mood.field.decay_per_hour.desc: How many points the mood drifts back toward calm each hour. Nobody carries one bad moment intact into the third day; 0 means no decay, and the mood stays wherever it was left.
plugin.mood.field.decay_per_hour.label: Points of decay per hour
plugin.mood.field.max_delta_per_call.des: How much one adjustment may move the mood, which sets how violently feelings swing. Lower makes them gradual; higher lets one sentence go from happy to devastated. Anything beyond is clamped, and the model is told so.
plugin.people.desc: People: the friends, family and colleagues in the character's life, each with a name, a relationship and a closeness that shifts as they spend time together; anyone the character mentions comes from here
plugin.people.field.max_inject_bytes.des: The list is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, relationships and recent news are dropped and only names and closeness remain; over it still, only the number of people is noted.
plugin.people.field.max_people.desc: How many people the book may hold. Past this, adding someone new is refused with a nudge to remove whoever is no longer around.
plugin.people.field.max_people.label: People limit
plugin.presence.desc: Presence: where the character is, what it is wearing, how it is sitting and what it is doing, kept as a snapshot injected each turn that survives compaction and new sessions
plugin.qq_bot.desc: Connects an official QQ bot for remote one-to-one sessions, with /new /status /compact /help and remote confirmation of dangerous operations
plugin.qq_bot.field.api_base.desc: Rarely needs changing. Note that the official sandbox does not support one-to-one chat; that only works once the bot is published
plugin.qq_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.qq_bot.field.app_id.desc: The AppID of your bot on the QQ open platform (the development settings page at q.qq.com)
plugin.qq_bot.field.app_id.label: AppID
plugin.qq_bot.field.app_secret.desc: The bot secret. It is kept on this machine only and never uploaded anywhere
plugin.qq_bot.field.app_secret.label: AppSecret
How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.qq_bot.field.format.desc: markdown: sent as native markdown messages (tables and images become text), falling back to plain text for that user if the platform refuses. Plain text: always converted to readable plain text first
plugin.qq_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.qq_bot.field.human_pace.desc: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.qq_bot.field.human_pace.label: Text like a person
plugin.qq_bot.field.merge_window_sec.des: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.qq_bot.field.push_notices.desc: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
plugin.qq_bot.field.push_notices.label: Push background notices
plugin.qq_bot.field.show_thinking.desc: Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.qq_bot.field.show_thinking.label: Show the thinking
plugin.qq_bot.field.show_tools.desc: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.qq_bot.field.show_tools.label: Show tool calls
plugin.qq_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One user_openid per line; only listed users get a reply, and an empty list refuses everyone. The first time a stranger writes, their openid is written to the log
plugin.qq_bot.field.whitelist.label: openid allowlist
plugin.read_file.desc: Reads the contents of a local text file
plugin.read_file.field.max_bytes.desc: Most bytes returned by one read; anything past this is truncated.
plugin.read_file.field.max_bytes.label: Maximum bytes read
plugin.relationship.desc: Relationship: what stage the two of you are at, what you call each other, what changed recently, and the understandings and the off-limits subjects, kept as a snapshot injected each turn so the character stops running hot and cold
plugin.roleplay.desc: Plays a character from your notes: injects the character sheet, sample lines and what it knows about you, acts out scenes and gestures in 【】, and holds the writing and the sense of time together
plugin.roleplay.field.boundaries.desc: Lets the character say no in its own voice: at the lightest, steering away from the subject; further along, naming what it feels and asking to stop; at the limit, refusing outright — always first person, always starting from a feeling. Where the line falls is decided by the character sheet and the scene, not by this plugin.
plugin.roleplay.field.boundaries.label: Allow boundaries
plugin.roleplay.field.failure_line.desc: The reply used when even generating a line fails (the provider being completely unreachable, for instance).
plugin.roleplay.field.failure_line.label: Fallback line
plugin.roleplay.field.humanize.desc: Suppresses the patterns that make Chinese read like a machine wrote it: "not X, but Y", the summarize-explain-summarize sandwich, transitional filler and polite sign-offs.
plugin.roleplay.field.humanize.label: Natural writing rules
plugin.roleplay.field.interaction.desc: Every reply opens with a 【】 block describing the scene, the action and the expression before anything is said; it may appear several times in one reply.
plugin.roleplay.field.interaction.label: Act out scenes in 【】
plugin.roleplay.field.max_text_bytes.des: Combined limit for the character sheet, what it knows about you, and the sample lines. All of it goes to the model in full every turn; over the limit they are kept in that order — sheet, then your profile, then samples.
plugin.roleplay.field.memory_rules.desc: Lets the character remember the way people do: everyday trivia fades, an old memory gets revised when the story changes, and recalling something means giving the gist rather than reciting the transcript — admitting it is hazy when it is.
plugin.roleplay.field.memory_rules.label: Memory and recall rules
plugin.roleplay.field.persona.desc: Who it is playing, what it is like, where it stands, how it talks. Injected every turn as the highest-priority prompt. Leave it empty to inject no character at all and keep only the writing rules.
plugin.roleplay.field.persona.label: Character sheet
plugin.roleplay.field.time_rules.desc: Anything about time is judged against the real clock now, not against a moment that appeared earlier in the history; the runtime environment (system, directories) stays out of the character's sense of self.
plugin.roleplay.field.time_rules.label: Time consistency rules
plugin.roleplay.field.translate_failures: When a model call fails — most often content stopped by the provider safety policy — turns it into a line in the character's voice, as if it had drifted off, and files the original error as a session note. Configuration errors (keys, addresses) are still reported verbatim. Requires a character sheet.
plugin.roleplay.field.user_profile.desc: Your basic circumstances, as something the character knows from the start. It can stay empty — tell it in conversation instead and let the memory plugin write it down.
plugin.roleplay.field.user_profile.label: About me
plugin.roleplay.field.voice_samples.desc: Samples of how the character actually talks, to anchor the voice — far more effective than describing a personality. Three to five exchanges works well, each a back and forth (what you say, how it answers), with a blank line between them; cover different moods (pleased, annoyed, talking about something serious), and if 【】 is on, use 【】 in the samples too. The people and events in the samples are only illustrations; the character does not take them as things that happened.
plugin.scene.desc: Scene: injects the setting as the stage for the acting, and keeps the places that come up in conversation as scene memories
plugin.scene.field.max_inject_bytes.desc: Scene memories are resent every turn, so they need a ceiling. Over the limit, descriptions are dropped and only names remain; over it still, only the number of scenes is noted.
plugin.scene.field.max_scenes.desc: Past this, the most recently updated are kept; the rest are still readable by the model and nothing is lost.
plugin.scene.field.max_scenes.label: Scenes injected
plugin.scene.field.stage.desc: The scene or environment the conversation happens in (place, era, atmosphere), injected each turn as the stage. Leave it empty to inject no fixed stage and only record scenes.
plugin.scene.field.stage.label: Setting
plugin.scheduler.desc: Creates scheduled tasks from within a conversation (one-off, recurring, daily), runs them in the background when their time comes and writes the result into the most recently active session
plugin.self_update.desc: Program updates: checks GitHub for new releases, and downloads, verifies, replaces and restarts from the settings page in one click
plugin.self_update.field.auto_check.desc: Ask GitHub for a new stable release on the schedule below. It only checks — nothing is downloaded or installed on its own, and whether to update is always your click here.
plugin.self_update.field.auto_restart.de: Restart the service as soon as the program file has been replaced, so the new version takes effect immediately. With this off the update still happens, but the new version waits until you start it yourself next time. Note that a restart interrupts any conversation in progress, and remote users have to sign in again afterwards.
plugin.self_update.field.check_hours.des: How long between checks. The time of the last check is recorded and survives a restart, so starting the program does not trigger a fresh check every time.
plugin.session_search.desc: Searches past conversations by keyword and date, transcripts included
plugin.session_search.field.max_archives: Before a session history is replaced by a summary it is archived verbatim, and searches cover the archives too; past this count the oldest are deleted. 0 disables archiving, and a compacted session then has only its summary left to search.
plugin.session_search.field.max_scan_ses: Searching means reading session files, newest first; sessions past this count are not read.
plugin.session_search.field.max_snippets: When one session matches in several places, how many excerpts to return.
plugin.skills.desc: Skills: lists the SKILL.md files in a directory, and the model reads the steps it needs on demand
plugin.skills.field.dir.desc: Where skills live, one subdirectory each. Leave it empty for the default (plugins/skills under the config directory); the rescan button below shows the full path in use.
plugin.skills.field.dir.label: Skills directory
plugin.skills.field.max_bytes.desc: Most bytes returned when reading one skill; anything past this is truncated.
plugin.skills.field.max_bytes.label: Maximum bytes per skill
plugin.skills.field.max_list.desc: How many skills the always-present list names. The rest do not disappear — the model can still see the full list for itself.
plugin.skills.field.max_list.label: Skills listed
plugin.style_watch.desc: Style watch: checks each reply for assistant-speak (calling itself an AI, pleasantries, filler, lists, bold, emoji) and tallies it by day; it measures without intervening
plugin.style_watch.field.ignore_rules.de: One rule id per line; ignored rules are neither counted nor flagged. Available rules: self_ai (calls itself an AI), opening_cliche (polite opener), flattery (fawning opener), closing_cliche (polite sign-off), transition_cliche (transitional filler), enumeration (first... second...), not_but (not X but Y), hedging (over-hedging), authority (vague appeal to authority), pseudo_analysis (fake analysis), promo_adjective (marketing tone), filler (filler words), summary_closing (summary sandwich), md_heading (headings), md_list (lists), md_bold (bold), emoji (emoji).
plugin.style_watch.field.notify.desc: Leaves a "style note" line in the current session when assistant-speak is detected. For your eyes only: it never enters the model context and never changes the reply. Several hits in one turn are merged into a single note.
plugin.style_watch.field.notify.label: Leave a session note on a hit
plugin.telegram_bot.desc: Connects a Telegram bot for remote one-to-one sessions, with /new /status /compact /help and remote confirmation of dangerous operations
plugin.telegram_bot.field.api_base.desc: Rarely needs changing. Set it if you run your own Bot API server or a reverse proxy
plugin.telegram_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.telegram_bot.field.bot_token.desc: The token you get from @BotFather with /newbot, shaped like 123456:ABC-DEF…. It is kept on this machine only and never uploaded anywhere
plugin.telegram_bot.field.confirm_timeou: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.telegram_bot.field.format.desc: markdown: converted to Telegram MarkdownV2, so bold and code blocks render properly, falling back to plain text for that user if parsing fails. Plain text: always converted to readable plain text first
plugin.telegram_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.telegram_bot.field.human_pace.des: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.telegram_bot.field.merge_window_s: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.telegram_bot.field.proxy.desc: api.telegram.org is unreachable directly on some networks. http, https and socks5 are supported, shaped like socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 or http://127.0.0.1:7890; leave it empty to connect directly
plugin.telegram_bot.field.proxy.label: Proxy address
plugin.telegram_bot.field.push_notices.d: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.telegram_bot.field.show_tools.des: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.telegram_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One chat_id per line (in a one-to-one chat this is your numeric user ID). Only listed users get a reply, and an empty list refuses everyone. Send the bot a message and its chat_id appears in the log
plugin.unspoken.desc: Unspoken: what the character has not said out loud — what it really thinks, what it is holding back, what it is waiting for — kept as a bounded list injected each turn that shapes its attitude and subtext without ever being read aloud
plugin.unspoken.field.max_entries.desc: How many things it can hold at once. When full, the oldest is let go automatically and the model is told so in the receipt.
plugin.unspoken.field.max_entries.label: Entry limit
plugin.unspoken.field.max_inject_bytes.d: The list is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, only the most recent entries are kept and the rest are noted as a count.
plugin.weather.desc: Weather: fetches the real weather for the configured cities on a timer and injects it each turn as part of the character's surroundings
plugin.weather.field.persona_location.de: Where the character lives, such as "Hangzhou" or "杭州". The weather on its side becomes part of its surroundings and its state. Leave it empty to inject nothing.
plugin.weather.field.refresh_minutes.des: How often to fetch in the background. Fetching more often does not produce fresher data, only more calls.
plugin.weather.field.same_city.desc: You are both in the same place. With this on, only the city above is queried and "city I am in" below has no effect.
plugin.weather.field.same_city.label: Same city as me
plugin.weather.field.stale_minutes.desc: Stop injecting weather this long after the last successful fetch. When nothing fresh can be had, it is better for the character not to know the weather than to treat a few hours ago as now. Must not be smaller than the refresh interval.
plugin.weather.field.stale_minutes.label: Stop injecting after (minutes)
From this hour on, tomorrow's forecast is in front of the character — during the day people think about today, and only look ahead near bedtime or when planning. Before that hour it glances at tomorrow only when you bring it up. 0 keeps it visible all day.
Hour to start looking at tomorrow
plugin.weather.field.user_location.desc: Where you are when the two of you are apart; the character knows what the weather is like on your side. Only in effect when the setting above is off; leave it empty to inject nothing.
plugin.weather.field.user_location.label: City I am in
plugin.web_fetch.desc: Fetches a web page and returns its text
plugin.web_fetch.field.max_bytes.desc: Most bytes read from one page; anything past this is truncated.
plugin.web_fetch.field.max_bytes.label: Maximum bytes fetched
plugin.web_fetch.field.timeout_seconds.d: Longest to wait for a single page.
plugin.wechat_bot.desc: Connects the official WeChat ClawBot plugin for remote one-to-one sessions on personal WeChat (bind by scanning a code in the settings page), with /new /status /compact /help and remote confirmation of dangerous operations
plugin.wechat_bot.field.api_base.desc: The entry point used to bind by QR code; it rarely needs changing. Once bound, requests go to the dedicated address the server hands out
plugin.wechat_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.wechat_bot.field.confirm_timeout_: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.wechat_bot.field.format.desc: markdown: sent as is, and the WeChat ClawBot interface renders bold, quotes and the like. Plain text: formatting marks are stripped before sending, which suits clients that show none
plugin.wechat_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.wechat_bot.field.human_pace.desc: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.wechat_bot.field.human_pace.label: Text like a person
plugin.wechat_bot.field.merge_window_sec: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.wechat_bot.field.push_notices.des: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
plugin.wechat_bot.field.show_thinking.de: Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.wechat_bot.field.show_tools.desc: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.wechat_bot.field.show_tools.label: Show tool calls
plugin.wechat_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One WeChat user ID per line (shaped like xxx@im.wechat). Whoever scanned the code to bind is always allowed; everyone else is refused, and their ID is written to the log so you can copy it in
plugin.wechat_bot.field.whitelist.label: User allowlist
